sections.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors (0:00-0:45)
sections.content: Recall that any 3D vector [x, y, z] is a linear combination of basis vectors i, j, k. Introduce the standard basis: i=[1,0,0], j=[0,1,0], k=[0,0,1].
sections.example: Imagine a 3D unit cube sitting at the origin; its corners define the reach of our basis vectors.

sections.title: Defining 3D Transformations (0:45-1:45)
sections.content: A linear transformation is defined by where the basis vectors i, j, and k land. We represent this as a 3x3 matrix where columns are the transformed vectors i', j', and k'.
sections.example: An animation shows i, j, and k stretching and rotating into new positions while the grid space deforms accordingly.

sections.title: Core Concept: The Determinant (1:45-3:00)
sections.content: The determinant of a 3x3 matrix represents the 'scaling factor' of volume. If the volume of a shape changes from V to V', the determinant is V'/V.
sections.example: A virtual 'Robo-Dog' model is inside a unit cube. As we apply a transformation matrix, the cube (and the dog) stretches; if the determinant is 2, the dog appears twice as large in volume.

sections.title: Application: Rotation & Shear (3:00-4:15)
sections.content: Explain that different matrices perform different geometric operations: Rotations (preserving lengths/volumes) vs. Shear (sliding layers) vs. Scaling.
sections.example: Use a character's arm: A rotation matrix rotates the elbow joint, while a shear matrix mimics the 'squash and stretch' effect used in 3D animation to express motion.

sections.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
sections.content: Recap: Any 3D linear transformation is simply a remapping of the 3D grid. The 3x3 matrix is the 'recipe' for where the foundation vectors end up.
sections.example: A quick montage: A complex 3D character mesh transforming through a sequence of matrix multiplications, showcasing the final smooth motion.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Review: Basis Vectors (0:00-0:45)
lecture_lines: Any 3D vector is a linear combination of basis vectors.
Meet the standard basis: i, j, and k vectors.
These define our 3D unit cube foundation.
animations: Fade in basis vectors i_hat (#FF5733) and j_hat (#33FF57).
Label i_hat and j_hat clearly near their vectors.
Highlight i_hat changing when scaled by a constant.
Animate the transformation of the unit square grid.
Change vector color to #FFFFFF to emphasize the result.

storyboard.title: Defining 3D Transformations (0:45-1:45)
lecture_lines: A linear transformation is defined by basis vector landing.
We represent this using a 3x3 matrix.
Columns show where i, j, and k move.
animations: Show a 3D grid with unit vectors i, j, k.
Animate a matrix multiplication acting on the 3D space.
Trace the path of the basis vectors under transformation.
Highlight the transformed volume using a faint color #3388FF.
Blink the final transformed basis vectors for emphasis.

storyboard.title: Core Concept: The Determinant (1:45-3:00)
lecture_lines: The determinant represents a scaling factor for volume.
Volume changes from V to V' under transformation.
Example: A matrix with determinant 2 doubles volume.
Stretching an object scales its total enclosed volume.
animations: Display a unit square and its transformation to a parallelogram.
Show the area calculation formula: det(M) = final_area.
Visualize the area expansion factor by scaling the square.
Highlight the area change with a fill color #FFFF33.
Show negative determinant flipping the orientation of the shape.

storyboard.title: Application: Rotation & Shear (3:00-4:15)
lecture_lines: Rotations preserve lengths and volumes in 3D.
Shear matrices create slide effects on grid layers.
Scaling transforms change overall dimensions of objects.
animations: Animate a 2D object rotating around the origin.
Display the rotation matrix components clearly near the object.
Visualize shear transformation shifting the object's sides.

storyboard.title: Summary & Synthesis (4:15-5:00)
lecture_lines: 3D transformations remap the entire 3D space grid.
The matrix is a recipe for basis movement.
Multiplication tracks complex character motion smoothly.
animations: Summarize key matrix transformation concepts visually.
Fade in the determinant formula again for final review.
Show the final combined matrix representation with labeled parts.
